defects.description: The out-of-order branch is entered when the new timestamp is greater than the latest instead of less, so normal in-order arrivals take the insert path that never advances `_latest_ts`; the window horizon freezes, nothing is ever evicted, and the sample set grows without bound.
paraphrases: The comparison meant to catch late (older) arrivals is reversed, so fresh newer samples are routed through the ordered-insert path that leaves the newest-timestamp watermark stuck at its first value and the trailing window stops sliding.
Because newer readings satisfy the `>` test, they bypass the branch that updates the high-water timestamp, so eviction's horizon never moves forward and stale points are retained indefinitely.

Detecting backfill should compare against `<`; flipping it to `>` means every in-sequence update is treated as a reorder, the latest-time marker is frozen, and the count keeps climbing past the window size.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        if self._latest_ts is not None and ts < self._latest_ts:'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The interpolated rank is scaled by `n` instead of `n - 1`, so interior percentiles land between the wrong pair of order statistics and return values shifted toward the upper end of the distribution.
paraphrases: Multiplying the fraction by the sample count rather than one less than it misplaces the fractional index, skewing every non-extreme percentile upward.
The linear-rank formula uses the wrong span: with `n` in place of `n-1`, the median and other quantiles interpolate at an offset position and come out too high.
Because the rank spans `n` intervals instead of the `n-1` gaps between ordered samples, the computed percentile picks a point further along the sorted values than intended.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        rank = (p / 100.0) * (n - 1)'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: `range_span` subtracts the maximum from the minimum, returning the negative of the true span rather than the documented `max - min`.
paraphrases: The two extremes are subtracted in the wrong order, so the reported spread is negated instead of being a non-negative width.
Computing smallest-minus-largest yields a negative magnitude for the window's range whenever the values are not all equal.
The span comes back with a flipped sign because the minuend and subtrahend are reversed.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        return max(values) - min(values)'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: Variance divides the sum of squared deviations by `n - 1`, producing the sample (Bessel-corrected) variance even though the method is documented to return the population variance (divide by `n`).
paraphrases: The estimator applies Bessel's correction, dividing by one fewer than the sample size, which contradicts the promised population-variance definition.
Using `n - 1` in the denominator overstates the spread relative to the population variance the docstring specifies.
The squared-deviation average is taken over `n - 1` rather than `n`, so the result is the unbiased sample variance instead of the intended population figure.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        return sum((v - mu) ** 2 for v in values) / n'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.
